name: Full House
summary: Three backs in a straight line across, all at the same depth. Perfectly balanced, perfectly symmetric, and the defense cannot tell from the alignment which of the three is getting it.
personnel: 11 players, 2 tight ends, quarterback, fullback, 2 halfbacks
notes: The full house T. Both ends are tight and on the line, and the three backs sit shoulder to shoulder four yards deep — left halfback, fullback, right halfback, evenly spaced. Nobody is offset and nobody is deeper, so the alignment gives away nothing. The formation is perfectly symmetric, so every play has a left and a right version off identical rules.
coaching_notes: The back digits are the same as the Wishbone on purpose — 2 is the fullback, 3 is the right halfback, 4 is the left halfback. A kid who has learned Bone calls already knows House calls.
Three backs at the same depth is the whole idea. In the Wishbone the fullback is closer than the halfbacks and a smart defense reads it. Here all three leave the same spot at the same time.
Every run uses all three backs: one carries, one kicks out, one leads through. Teach the three jobs, not the three plays — then the same three jobs work in both directions.
Count seven on the line every snap. There is no flanker or wing to creep up here, so this is the formation least likely to get you an illegal formation flag.
Symmetric formation, symmetric rules — the kids learn one play and get two.
